title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the previous and following pages. X is a curve (or variety) over a field K, and Γ = Gal(K̄/K). I is a set of base points: rational points of X and/or tangential points 'at infinity'. Π̂_1(X, I) is the profinite fundamental groupoid with base set I. Θ is a 'virtual' (abstract) group acting on Π̂_1(X, I), with lifted actions Θ' on Π̂_1(X', I') for finite covers X' → X, where I' = X'|I. The question is which such Θ are 'effective', i.e. come from the natural Galois action of Γ.

The previous page lists necessary conditions:
- 2°) Certain subgroups of π_1(X, x) are stable.
- 3°) For a morphism f: X' → Y and x' ∈ X'_K ∩ I', the induced action of Θ'_{x'} on π̂_1(X', x') stabilizes ker(π̂_1(X', x') → π̂_1(Y, f(x'))).
- 4°) For two finite covers X'_1, X'_2 and a morphism f: X'_1 → X'_2 (not necessarily over X), with J = I'_1 ∩ f^{-1}(I'_2) ≠ ∅, the map Π̂_1(X'_1, J) → Π̂_1(X'_2, I'_2) is Θ-equivariant.

This page:
1. Grothendieck notes that 3°) and 4°) can be merged into a condition 5°). Take a correspondence X'_1 →f_1 Y ←f_2 X'_2 where f_2 induces surjections on π_1 (fibration-like, connected fibres). Then Π̂_1(Y, f_2(I'_2)) is a quotient of Π̂_1(X'_2, I'_2).
2. 5°) requires that the action Θ'_2 descend to this quotient (this is 3°) and that the resulting action on Π̂_1(Y, ·) be compatible with f_1 (this is 4°). He adds that this would even subsume 2°).
3. He doubts he needs this generality. He then states the real issue: conditions 2°–4° are not the truly natural way to obtain necessary conditions on the 'virtual parameters' for them to be effective (coming from Γ, with Γ 'indeterminate').
4. The real point is to find necessary AND sufficient conditions characterizing the Θ coming from Γ.

In modern terms, this asks for the image of Gal(K̄/K) inside the automorphisms of the system of profinite fundamental groupoids of all covers of X, compatible with all algebraic morphisms and correspondences among them. This is exactly the shape of the Ihara / Oda–Matsumoto question ('Galois = motivic automorphisms of π_1'). The next page goes on to define T-horizontal paths and cocycles g^T(u) for real/topological base sets T.
errors: Not an error but a gap: for the quotient to make sense, f_2 must induce surjections on π̂_1 for every base point used. In practice this needs geometrically connected (generic) fibres, and connectedness conditions on f_2(I'_2) analogous to J ≠ ∅ in 4°). These are not spelled out.
Θ acts on groupoids (or up to inner automorphisms) and is lifted to covers via Θ'. 5°) implicitly needs the lifts Θ'_1 and Θ'_2 chosen compatibly; this choice issue is left implicit.

ideas.what: Combined condition 5°): equivariance of the profinite fundamental groupoid under correspondences X'_1 → Y ← X'_2, with f_2 π_1-surjective, so the action descends to the quotient Π̂_1(Y) and is compatible with f_1.
ideas.modern_name: Compatibility of automorphisms with all morphisms/correspondences of the fundamental-group system (Oda–Matsumoto type 'motivic' automorphisms)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara (ICM 1990) and Oda–Matsumoto (1990s); 'finite tripod' I/OM resolved by F. Pop (2010s)
ideas.where_published: Not in Esquisse d'un programme in this form; Esquisse discusses the Teichmüller tower and GT-type conditions instead.

ideas.what: Programmatic aim: necessary and sufficient conditions characterizing which abstract actions Θ on Π̂_1(X, I), with lifts to all finite covers, come from Gal(K̄/K).
ideas.modern_name: Galois-theoretic characterization of Gal(K̄/K) inside Aut/Out of geometric fundamental groups (I/OM; GT-type descriptions)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara, Oda, Matsumoto; Drinfeld (GT, 1990); Pop; Hoshi–Minamide–Mochizuki
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) states the related goal of describing Gal(Q̄/Q) via its action on the Teichmüller tower. The single-variety, all-covers, groupoid-with-base-set formulation does not appear there.

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates, probably around 1981, the problem later called the Ihara/Oda–Matsumoto question: characterize Galois actions as those automorphisms of the profinite fundamental groupoids of all finite covers that respect all algebraic morphisms and correspondences (kernel-stability 3°, equivariance 4°, combined 5°). He uses groupoids with sets of (tangential/rational) base points, and explicitly seeks necessary and sufficient conditions.
missed.quote: Le point est réellement de dégager des conditions néc. et suff. qui permettent de caractériser les Θ provenant de Γ
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives an earlier provenance for the I/OM circle of ideas, which is usually credited to Ihara and Oda–Matsumoto around 1990. The groupoid version with base sets I, and correspondences X'_1 → Y ← X'_2 as the basic compatibility, is a slightly different formulation from Pop's tripod version and might be of interest.

missed.claim: Grothendieck judges conditions 2°–4° 'not really natural' and leaves open what the natural necessary-and-sufficient conditions should be. The next page turns to T-horizontal paths over real/topological loci, i.e. a different, real-structure-type condition.
missed.quote: Les conditions 2° : 4° ne sont pas vraiment les conditions réellement naturelles
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a still-relevant open methodological question: which compatibility system cuts out exactly the Galois image, for a single curve over a general field K, without passing to all varieties.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a programmatic remark rather than a result. Its interest is that it sets out, early and in groupoid form, a functorial characterization of Galois-coming actions that anticipates the Ihara/Oda–Matsumoto question, a framing not visible in Grothendieck's published texts.
transcription_corrections: The groupoids are written with a capital Π̂_1 (Π̂_1(Y, f_2(I'_2)), Π̂_1(X'_2, I'_2)), not lowercase π̂_1.

The opening line reads 'À vrai dire, il ne serait pas difficile de dégager une condition 5°) qui mette ensemble 3°) et 4°), quand on se donne non X'_1 → X'_2, mais' followed by the diagram X'_1 →f_1 Y, X'_2 →f_2 Y.

'avec f_2 induisant des homs surjectifs sur les Π_1, de sorte que Π̂_1(Y, f_2(I'_2)) peut s'interpréter comme un quotient de Π̂_1(X'_2, I'_2), et soit que l'action Θ'_2 de Θ sur ce dernier passe au quotient Π̂_1(Y, f_2(I'_2))'.
Probable reading: '(et = de 2°, 3°, 4°, à vrai dire !)', i.e. the generalization would cover 2°, 3° and 4°.
